# Every setting and its default

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_variable_reference.py from roles/*/defaults/main.yml. Do not edit by hand:
     change the comment in the role's defaults file and run the script. -->

This page lists **every setting a role reads**, with the value it has when you set nothing, and
what the role's own comment says. It is generated from `roles/<role>/defaults/main.yml`, so it is
never out of date. Where to put a setting, and which place wins when it is in two, is in
[VARIABLES.md](VARIABLES.md). Values are shortened to one line here: the role file has the full one.

A setting that is a list (`[a, b]`) **replaces** the default list when you set it; it does not add
to it. Repeat the entries you want to keep.

**Contents:** [aap_email_question](#aap_email_question), [ad_lockout](#ad_lockout), [ad_report](#ad_report), [cert_inventory](#cert_inventory), [check_accounts](#check_accounts), [check_auditd](#check_auditd), [check_certs](#check_certs), [check_containers](#check_containers), [check_disk](#check_disk), [check_fapolicyd](#check_fapolicyd), [check_logging](#check_logging), [check_mariadb](#check_mariadb), [check_mounts](#check_mounts), [check_network](#check_network), [check_patching](#check_patching), [check_performance](#check_performance), [check_selinux](#check_selinux), [check_services](#check_services), [check_sso](#check_sso), [check_stig](#check_stig), [check_time](#check_time), [check_trust](#check_trust), [horizon](#horizon), [log_analysis](#log_analysis), [net_certs](#net_certs), [net_config](#net_config), [net_perf](#net_perf), [ontap_report](#ontap_report), [patch](#patch), [poam](#poam), [podman_discover](#podman_discover), [service_watch](#service_watch), [servicenow](#servicenow), [site_act](#site_act), [site_email](#site_email), [site_findings](#site_findings), [stigman_stack](#stigman_stack), [troubleshoot](#troubleshoot), [vmware_vm](#vmware_vm), [win_act](#win_act), [win_check_accounts](#win_check_accounts), [win_check_audit](#win_check_audit), [win_check_certs](#win_check_certs), [win_check_disk](#win_check_disk), [win_check_eventlog](#win_check_eventlog), [win_check_network](#win_check_network), [win_check_patching](#win_check_patching), [win_check_performance](#win_check_performance), [win_check_security](#win_check_security), [win_check_services](#win_check_services), [win_check_time](#win_check_time), [win_check_trust](#win_check_trust), [win_patch](#win_patch), [win_troubleshoot](#win_troubleshoot), [settings of one host](#settings-of-one-host)

## aap_email_question

File: `roles/aap_email_question/defaults/main.yml`

> THE "ALSO EMAIL THE REPORT TO" QUESTION (playbooks/aap_email_question.yml): adds a text box to the survey of every report template and of the workflows that run them, through AAP's API, so whoever launches one can send that run's report to more people (report_email_also, added to the template's report_email_to). Run it once, and again after you add report templates. docs/EMAIL_REPORTS.md, "Also email the report to".

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `aap_email_question_state` | `present` | present = add the question; absent = take it out again |
| `aap_email_question_playbooks` | `- act_fix_approved.yml - ad_health_report.yml - ad_lockout.yml - cert_report.yml - databa…` | Which templates: the job templates whose playbook is one of these (the file name - your template names do not matter). Every playbook that can email a report is here; a test keeps the list complete. |
| `aap_email_question_templates` | `[]` | more job templates or workflows, by name or ID |
| `aap_email_question_exclude` | `[]` | templates left out, by name or ID |
| `aap_email_question_workflows` | `true` | also the workflows that run them (a job in a workflow is never asked its own survey) |
| `aap_email_question_project` | (empty) | only job templates of this AAP project (its name); empty = any project |
| `aap_email_question_ca_path` | (empty) | a CA file for AAP's HTTPS certificate ("" = what the execution environment trusts) |
| `aap_email_question_text` | `Also email the report to` | The question, as whoever launches a template sees it. A text box of several lines (a pasted list keeps its line breaks), not required, empty by default. |
| `aap_email_question_description` | (worked out by the role; see its file) | The help text under the question. |

## ad_lockout

File: `roles/ad_lockout/defaults/main.yml`

> Account lockout (playbooks/ad_lockout.yml): is the account locked out, and WHAT is locking it out - the computers its bad passwords came from, from the Security log of every domain controller. Read-only, unless ad_lockout_unlock. A PowerShell script on every DC (WinRM, the Windows Machine credential): the account needs to read the DCs' Security logs - see docs/ACTIVE_DIRECTORY.md, "Account lockout".

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ad_lockout_user` | (empty) | The account to look at, as the service desk is given it: jdoe, CORP\jdoe or jdoe@corp.example.mil (a survey question, NOT required). Several: one per line, or separated by commas. "" = every account locked out now, each with the computer locking it out. |
| `ad_lockout_hours` | `24` | the Security log entries of the last this-many hours (raise it for a lockout of last week) |
| `ad_lockout_max_users` | `25` | at most this many accounts (asked for, or locked out now) in one run |
| `ad_lockout_unlock` | `false` | true = unlock the account (on the PDC emulator) after reading - only an account asked for by name, and only when it is locked out. A dry run (Check) says what it would unlock. It locks out again as soon as the source computer tries its old password again: the report says what to fix first. |
| `ad_lockout_check_sources` | `false` | true = also look on each source computer that is a host of this job's inventory (Windows, WinRM, the same credential - it needs administrator rights there): services and scheduled tasks running as the account, its sessions (a disconnected Remote Desktop session), processes and mapped drives. Read-only. |
| `ad_lockout_check_max` | `5` | look on at most this many source computers per account (the worst first) |
| `ad_lockout_exchange_servers` | `[]` | Your mail servers (Exchange / ActiveSync, by name or address, * and ? allowed, e.g. [EXCH*, 192.0.2.25]): bad passwords coming through one of them are a phone or a mail app with the old password. |
| `ad_lockout_max_events` | `2000` | ---- How much is read ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ read at most this many Security log entries per account and DC (the newest) |
| `ad_lockout_resolve_max` | `50` | resolve at most this many addresses to names per DC (reverse DNS) |
| `ad_lockout_max_rows` | `50` | rows per table; the job's artifacts (ad_lockout) have all |

## ad_report

File: `roles/ad_report/defaults/main.yml`

> Active Directory health report (playbooks/ad_health_report.yml). Read-only: a PowerShell script on every domain controller (WinRM, the Windows Machine credential) and one more on one DC per domain. The account needs to read AD and run dcdiag / repadmin on the DCs: see docs/ACTIVE_DIRECTORY.md.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ad_report_hours` | `24` | ---- Changes ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ the changes of the last this-many hours (match it to the schedule: a daily job = 24) |
| `ad_event_hours` | `24` | the event log entries of the last this-many hours |
| `ad_security_events` | `true` | read each DC's Security log for WHO made a change (needs auditing of account and security group management) |
| `ad_max_events` | `2000` | read at most this many entries per event log and DC |
| `ad_changes_max` | `500` | look at most at this many changed objects per kind (created, changed accounts, GPO links) |
| `ad_privileged_groups_extra` | `[DnsAdmins]` | Privileged groups watched besides the built-in ones (Domain / Enterprise / Schema Admins, Administrators, Account / Server / Print / Backup Operators, Group Policy Creator Owners, Key Admins, Cert Publishers): names or SIDs of this domain's groups. |
| `ad_groups_should_be_empty` | `[]` | privileged groups that must have no member, e.g. [Schema Admins] - amber when they have one |
| `ad_privileged_change_severity` | `warning` | a member added to / removed from a privileged group: warning, critical or info |
| `ad_schema_change_severity` | `warning` | the schema version changed: warning, critical or info |
| `ad_dc_change_severity` | `info` | a domain controller added or removed: warning, critical or info |
| `ad_dcdiag_skip` | `[SystemLog]` | ---- What is read on each DC --------------------------------------------------------------------- dcdiag tests to skip (SystemLog fails on any error in the System log: the Events table covers it) |
| `ad_dcdiag_dns` | `true` | also dcdiag's DNS tests that only read (basic, forwarders, delegation, record registration) |
| `ad_trust_verify` | `true` | verify outbound and two-way trusts (nltest /sc_verify) |
| `ad_repl_warn_hours` | `6` | ---- Thresholds: at or above "warn" = amber, at or above "crit" = red ------------------------------ a replication link with no success for this long (inter-site schedules: keep above their interval) |
| `ad_repl_crit_hours` | `24` | no success for this long (or a failing link) -> red |
| `ad_repl_queue_warn` | `50` | replication requests waiting in a DC's inbound queue |
| `ad_time_warn_seconds` | `5` | a DC's clock against the PDC emulator (the PDC: against its NTP source) |
| `ad_time_crit_seconds` | `60` | clock offset -> red (Kerberos fails at 300) |
| `ad_time_sync_warn_hours` | `24` | Windows Time last synchronized longer ago than this |
| `ad_disk_warn_pct` | `15` | free space of the database, log and SYSVOL volumes, % (at or below) |
| `ad_disk_crit_pct` | `5` | free % -> red |
| `ad_cert_warn_days` | `30` | the LDAPS / KDC certificate expires within this many days |
| `ad_cert_crit_days` | `7` | expires within this many days -> red |
| `ad_backup_warn_days` | `7` | the last system-state backup of a partition is older than this |
| `ad_backup_crit_days` | `30` | older than this -> red (always red past the tombstone lifetime) |
| `ad_krbtgt_max_days` | `180` | the krbtgt password is older than this -> amber (the STIG asks for 180) |
| `ad_rid_warn_pct` | `10` | RID pool left, % (at or below) |
| `ad_rid_crit_pct` | `2` | RID pool left -> red |
| `ad_no_client_site_warn` | `1` | this many client addresses in no AD subnet -> amber (fewer: blue) |
| `ad_report_max_rows` | `50` | rows per table (problems first); the job's artifacts have all |
| `ad_report_fail` | `false` | The job stays green when it finds problems: the report and email say what. true = mark it FAILED when there is a critical finding or a DC could not be read, for workflows. |

## cert_inventory

File: `roles/cert_inventory/defaults/main.yml`

> CERTIFICATE INVENTORY: every certificate report (Linux, Windows, VMware, network devices) can also write what it found - every certificate, with the same fields from each - for a dashboard (Power BI ...). Two ways, each on by itself: files (CSV + JSON) and a SQL Server table. A Check run writes nothing. The fields: id, source, host, location, subject, issuer, sans, not_after, days, status, tier (root / intermediate / ca-signed / self-signed), trust_store, in_use, public_key, sig_alg, serial, sha1, sha256, scanned_at, job (docs/CERT_INVENTORY.md).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `cert_inventory_files` | `false` | ---- files: <source>-certificates.csv and .json (source: linux, windows, vmware, net), replaced each run ---- true = write the files |
| `cert_inventory_dir` | `/var/lib/site-automation/cert-inventory` | where: on the AAP node the job runs on (a path AAP exposes to jobs: docs/CERT_INVENTORY.md), or on cert_inventory_host |
| `cert_inventory_host` | (empty) | an inventory host to write them on instead (a file server, or a Linux host with the share mounted); its credential must be on the job template |
| `cert_inventory_history` | `false` | true = also a dated copy (<source>-certificates-YYYY-MM-DD.csv) next to them, for trends |
| `cert_inventory_sql` | `false` | The login comes from the "SQL Server (certificate inventory)" credential (aap/credential_types/cert_inventory_sql.yml). The execution environment needs pymssql and community.general (the all-in-one EE has both). true = add / update the rows |
| `cert_inventory_sql_server` | (empty) | the SQL Server (name or address) |
| `cert_inventory_sql_port` | `1433` | its port |
| `cert_inventory_sql_database` | (empty) | the database (SQL Server 2016 or later: the rows go in as JSON, OPENJSON) |
| `cert_inventory_sql_table` | `dbo.cert_inventory` | schema.table |
| `cert_inventory_sql_create` | `false` | true = create the table (and its view <table>_current) when it is not there - the account then needs CREATE TABLE |

## check_accounts

File: `roles/check_accounts/defaults/main.yml`

> ACCOUNTS: the account problems auditors and attackers both look for, plus the one that quietly breaks automation - a service account password about to expire.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_accounts_min_uid` | `1000` | people's accounts start here |
| `check_accounts_inactive_days` | `35` | the STIG wants unused accounts disabled after 35 days |
| `check_accounts_ignore_inactive` | `[]` | Accounts that may stay unused (break-glass, service accounts that never log in interactively) |
| `check_accounts_nopasswd_allowed` | `[]` | sudoers entries allowed to use NOPASSWD, e.g. the account AAP connects as: [svc_aap, "%wheel"] |
| `check_accounts_expiry_watch` | `[]` | Accounts whose password/account expiry matters - above all the account AAP logs in with. e.g. [svc_aap] |
| `check_accounts_expiry_warn_days` | `14` | a watched account's password or account expiring within this many days -> warning (3 days or less -> critical) |

## check_auditd

File: `roles/check_auditd/defaults/main.yml`

> AUDITD: the audit system records who did what (the STIG depends on it). Running, enabled in the kernel, rules loaded, no events lost, room for its log, and (optionally) forwarding. Also how MUCH it records: too much rotates the evidence away within hours, fills the disk (then auditd stops the host or puts it in single-user mode, as the STIG sets it up), drops records on the way to the SIEM, and uses up the SIEM licence.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_auditd_min_rules` | `5` | fewer loaded rules than this = the STIG rules are missing |
| `check_auditd_log_warn_pct` | `75` | the audit log's filesystem |
| `check_auditd_log_crit_pct` | `90` | % used of that filesystem -> critical (warning from check_auditd_log_warn_pct) |
| `check_auditd_remote_required` | `false` | true = au-remote (audisp-remote) must be active |
| `check_auditd_exclude_accounts` | `[]` | Accounts whose audit events are expected in bulk and do NOT count toward the volume warning, e.g. the account a vulnerability scanner logs in with (a credentialed scan runs thousands of commands with sudo). Names or UIDs; a host that does not have the account skips it. The report still says how much they made, and the… (all of it: the role file) |
| `check_auditd_volume_hours` | `24` | look at the audit records of the last N hours |
| `check_auditd_volume_warn_mb_day` | `200` | warning above this many MB of audit records a day (excluded accounts not counted) |
| `check_auditd_retention_warn_hours` | `24` | With max_log_file_action ROTATE, auditd keeps num_logs files of max_log_file MB and deletes the oldest. Warning when what is left on disk reaches back fewer hours than this. The STIG wants a week (168) when the records are NOT sent off the host as they are written (RHEL-08-030660). 0 = off. |
| `check_auditd_volume_timeout` | `120` | The breakdown (which account, which rule, which program) reads the audit log files of the window at low CPU and disk priority, and only when the volume or the retention is over its limit. It stops after this many seconds on a host with very large logs (and says so). |

## check_certs

File: `roles/check_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> CERTS: certificates that expire soon - as files on the host, inside Java keystores, and as served by TLS endpoints (what a browser or client actually sees).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_certs_warn_days` | `30` | a certificate expiring within this many days -> warning (and amber in the certificate report) |
| `check_certs_notice_days` | `60` | the certificate report colours these blue (an early heads-up; not a finding) |
| `check_certs_crit_days` | `14` | within this many days (or expired) -> critical |
| `check_certs_files` | `[]` | Certificate files (PEM) to check. Globs work. Every certificate in a file is checked (a chain file with an expiring intermediate is a problem too). e.g. [/etc/stigman/*.crt, /etc/pki/tls/certs/server.crt] |
| `check_certs_discover` | `true` | Also look for certificates in the usual places. Files with many certificates are CA bundles (hundreds of roots, noisy) and are skipped unless listed in check_certs_files. Text (PEM) and binary (DER) certificates are both read; the names in any case (.crt, .CRT, .Pem ...). |
| `check_certs_discover_dirs` | `[/etc/pki/tls/certs, /etc/pki/nginx, /etc/nginx, /etc/httpd/conf.d, /etc/stigman, /etc/st…` | the folders searched (two levels deep) for *.crt, *.pem, *.cer, *.der (/etc/stigman/nginx/tls: STIG Manager's nginx certificate, three levels down) |
| `check_certs_discover_extra_dirs` | `[]` | more folders searched the same way, added to the ones above (no need to repeat them), e.g. [/home, /root, /opt/app/certs] |
| `check_certs_discover_exclude` | `'ca-bundle\|ca-certificates\|/localhost\.crt$'` | regular expression: found files whose path matches are skipped |

## check_disk

File: `roles/check_disk/defaults/main.yml`

> DISK: how full each LOCAL filesystem is (space and inodes), and - from the history of earlier runs - how many days until it is full. Network filesystems (NFS) are the mounts check's job: a hung NFS server can make `df` hang, so this check never touches them.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_disk_warn_pct` | `85` | % used -> warning |
| `check_disk_crit_pct` | `95` | % used -> critical |
| `check_disk_inode_warn_pct` | `85` | inodes: too many small files fill a disk too |
| `check_disk_inode_crit_pct` | `95` | % of inodes used -> critical (warning from check_disk_inode_warn_pct) |
| `check_disk_overrides` | `{}` | Different limits for particular mount points, e.g. keep the audit log partition emptier: check_disk_overrides: /var/log/audit: {warn: 70, crit: 85} |
| `check_disk_ignore` | `- '^/(proc\|sys\|dev\|run)(/\|$)' - '^/etc/(hosts\|hostname\|resolv\.conf)$' # bind-mounted fil…` | Mount points to skip (regular expressions). |
| `check_disk_exclude_types` | `[tmpfs, devtmpfs, squashfs, overlay, iso9660, efivarfs, nsfs]` | filesystem types never checked (df -x) |
| `check_disk_forecast` | `true` | Days-until-full forecast. Each run adds a sample (date, bytes used) per mount to a small file on the host; once there is at least a day of history, the growth rate predicts when the filesystem fills. Check mode (a dry run) reads the history but does not add to it. |
| `check_disk_forecast_warn_days` | `14` | full within this many days at the current growth -> warning |
| `check_disk_forecast_crit_days` | `3` | full within this many days -> critical |
| `check_disk_history_file` | `/var/lib/site-health/disk-history.json` | where the forecast keeps its samples, on the host |
| `check_disk_history_keep_days` | `30` | samples older than this are dropped (the forecast uses what is left) |
| `check_disk_timeout` | `20` | seconds for df |

## check_sso

File: `roles/check_sso/defaults/main.yml`

> SSO (read-only): can domain users still log in? A Linux host joined to Active Directory or IdM (sssd, realmd, winbind) keeps working on cached logins for a while after it loses its domain - then logins fail. A host that is not joined to any domain is skipped.

| `check_sso_kdc_warn` | `3` | "cannot contact any KDC" this many times -> warning |
| `check_sso_keytab` | `/etc/krb5.keytab` | the host's keytab |
| `check_sso_keytab_test` | `true` | get a ticket with it (kinit -k into memory: nothing is written) - proves the machine account works |
| `check_sso_testjoin` | `true` | adcli testjoin on hosts joined to Active Directory with adcli / realmd |
| `check_sso_test_users` | `[]` | domain users that must resolve (getent passwd), e.g. [svc_monitor@example.mil]; empty = none |
| `check_sso_sssd_dir` | `/etc/sssd` | sssd's configuration (sssd.conf, conf.d/): there = sssd is set up |
| `check_sso_smb_conf` | `/etc/samba/smb.conf` | Samba's: security = ads there = winbind is set up for Active Directory |
| `check_sso_sssd_log_dir` | `/var/log/sssd` | sssd's own logs, read with the journal |
| `check_sso_timeout` | `30` | seconds for each command that asks the domain (kinit, adcli, getent) |

## check_trust

File: `roles/check_trust/defaults/main.yml`

> TRUST (read-only): which trust stores on the host still hold a certificate authority that was compromised or that the browsers dropped - the system bundles, p11-kit's live view and blocklist, Java cacerts, Python's certifi bundles, Node's built-in roots, the bundles inside running podman containers, certificate files an application carries - and the software with its own trust logic (Go programs, Node, NSS) below the version that fixed it. The list of certificates to look for ships with the check (roles/check_trust/vars/main.yml: October 2026, the eight eMudhra intermediates and their roots); add your own in check_trust_extra. The health check runs it in the weekly set; playbooks/trust_report.yml runs it on every host, vCenter and ESXi too.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_trust_extra` | `[]` | More certificates to look for, besides the shipped list: name, sha256 (the certificate's fingerprint, with or without colons), spki_sha256 (its public key, optional), kind (root / intermediate), severity (critical / warning / notice), why. Get the fingerprints with: openssl x509 -in the.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256… (all of it: the role file) |
| `check_trust_severity` | `{}` | another severity for a listed name: {"AAA Certificate Services": warning} once you decide to blocklist it; notice = listed only, no finding |
| `check_trust_software_severity` | `warning` | the finding for a program below the fixed version (a Go program, Node, NSS): warning or critical |
| `check_trust_bundles` | `[/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem, /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/openssl/c…` | The system: the CA bundles every OpenSSL / Go / Python client reads (the ones that exist are read), p11-kit's live view (trust extract: what NSS and GnuTLS clients see, and the blocklist), the blocklist folders. the system CA bundles (RHEL, Debian / Ubuntu, Alpine, SUSE); the same file under two names is read once |
| `check_trust_blocklist_dirs` | `[/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/blocklist, /usr/share/pki/ca-trust-source/blocklist]` | p11-kit blocklist folders: a certificate there is distrusted (listed as blocked, no finding) |
| `check_trust_p11kit` | `true` | read p11-kit's live anchors and blocklist too (trust extract), when the trust command is there |
| `check_trust_nss_dirs` | `[/etc/pki/nssdb, /root/.pki/nssdb, /home/*/.pki/nssdb]` | NSS databases read with certutil (the system's: curl and other NSS clients on older RHEL; root's and each user's: Chrome, Evolution) |
| `check_trust_ca_certificates_fixed` | (empty) | the ca-certificates package version that dropped the roots, e.g. '2026.2.82' (empty: not compared - the bundles themselves tell) |

| `check_trust_java` | `true` | Java: every cacerts / jssecacerts under these folders (JDKs, and the keystores of running java programs), read directly (JKS) or with keytool (PKCS12), with the JDK's version. |
| `check_trust_java_dirs` | `[/usr/lib/jvm, /usr/java, /etc/pki/java, /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/java, /opt, /usr/loc…` | folders searched for cacerts (seven levels deep) |
| `check_trust_python` | `true` | Python: every certifi bundle (certifi/cacert.pem: requests, pip, urllib3 ... carry their own roots, not the system's) under these folders - system Python, venvs, applications. |
| `check_trust_python_dirs` | `[/usr/lib, /usr/lib64, /usr/local, /opt, /srv, /var/lib, /root, /home]` | folders searched for certifi/cacert.pem (twelve levels deep) |
| `check_trust_node` | `true` | Node: its built-in roots (not the system's: Node carries its own, unless started with --use-openssl-ca), and its version against the one that dropped the root, per major line. |
| `check_trust_node_paths` | `[/usr/local/bin/node, /usr/local/node*/bin/node, /opt/*/bin/node, /opt/node*/bin/node, /r…` | where node binaries are (globs); the one in PATH and running ones are found too |
| `check_trust_node_fixed` | `{"22": "22.23.4", "24": "24.22.1", "26": "26.12.1"}` | Node's fixed version per major line (an older line than the oldest listed: unsupported, no fix) |

Go 1.27.3 / 1.26.10 reject any chain with one of the compromised keys (CVE-2026-111943) - a program built with an older Go has to be rebuilt. The running programs, and the executables under these folders, with the Go version each was built with. |

OFF by default - a read-only report. Check mode shows what would go and changes nothing. The system trust is blocklisted (RHEL / SUSE: a P… (all of it: the role file) |
| `check_trust_remove_kinds` | `[system, java, python, file, nssdb]` | which kinds of store to change: system (blocklist), java (every keystore), python (certifi), file (an application's bundle or certificate file), nssdb (certutil -D) |
| `check_trust_remove_severities` | `[critical, warning]` | only certificates at these severities go; a notice-level one (AAA Certificate Services) never, unless named here |
| `check_trust_remove_backup_dir` | `/var/backups/site-automation/trust` | every file changed is copied here first (a folder per run) |

## horizon

> VMware Horizon 8 (playbooks/horizon_*.yml): the Connection Server's REST API, from the AAP side, with the "Horizon API" credential (its address, domain, user name and password) - no collection needed. Every job asks each API path at the newest version first, down to v1, so it fits any Horizon 8 release. A dry run (Check) reads and says what it would do; it changes nothing. docs/HORIZON.md

| `horizon_page_size` | `500` | records per page when reading pools, desktops and sessions (Horizon's most: 1000) |
| `horizon_api_newest` | `9` | the newest API version to try (v9 down to v1): the first that answers is used |
| `horizon_action_version` | `v1` | the API version of the actions (reset, recover, log off, push image...) |
| `horizon_protected_pools` | `[]` | ---- Pools no job changes ----------------------------------------------------------------------- Desktop pools no job fixes, logs off or pushes an image to: names as Horizon Console shows them, * and ? allowed, any case (e.g. [VIP-*, Kiosk]). The reports still show them. |
| `horizon_cert_warn_days` | `30` | ---- Health report (playbooks/horizon_health_report.yml) ---------------------------------------- a Connection Server's, gateway's or vCenter's certificate expires within this many days -> amber |
| `horizon_cert_crit_days` | `7` | within this many days (or expired, or not valid) -> red |
| `horizon_license_warn_days` | `60` | the license expires within this many days -> amber |
| `horizon_report_max_rows` | `50` | rows in the problems table (the job's artifacts have all) |
| `horizon_health_fail` | `false` | The health and capacity reports stay green when they find problems: the report says what. true = mark the job FAILED on a critical finding, for workflows and alerts. |
| `horizon_capacity_warn_pct` | `80` | ---- Capacity report (playbooks/horizon_capacity_report.yml) ------------------------------------ a pool's desktops in use (connected or disconnected) against its maximum, % -> amber |
| `horizon_capacity_crit_pct` | `95` | in use, % -> red (also red: no free desktop left) |
| `horizon_broken_states` | `[AGENT_UNREACHABLE, AGENT_ERR_DISABLED, AGENT_ERR_INVALID_IP, AGENT_ERR_NEED_REBOOT, AGEN…` | ---- Broken desktops (the desktops check -> approval -> the fix job) ---------------------------- A desktop in one of these states takes no user until it is fixed. Left out on purpose: states that pass by themselves (being made, customized, deleted, waiting for the agent at start-up, maintenance). |
| `horizon_desktops_mode` | `report` | report = the check lists them and stays green (a schedule). approval = when there is a desktop to fix, the check hands the list on and FAILS on purpose, so the workflow takes its "Run on fail" path to the approval step and then the fix job. Set approval on the workflow's check node. |
| `horizon_fix_default_action` | `recover` | what fixes a broken desktop: recover (instant clones: deleted and made again from the image), reset, restart, remove, rebuild |

| `horizon_fix_max` | `20` | fix at most this many desktops per run: the rest are listed, the next run takes them |
| `horizon_fix_exclude_machines` | `[]` | desktops never fixed automatically: names, * and ? allowed (e.g. [W11-TEST-*]) |
| `horizon_session_max_disconnected_hours` | `8` | ---- Disconnected sessions (playbooks/horizon_session_cleanup.yml) ------------------------------ log off a session disconnected for this many hours or more |
| `horizon_session_cleanup_max` | `100` | log off at most this many sessions per run |
| `horizon_session_cleanup_exclude_pools` | `[]` | pools whose sessions are never logged off: names, * and ? allowed |
| `horizon_session_cleanup_exclude_users` | `[]` | users never logged off: login names (jdoe or CORP\jdoe) or SIDs |
| `horizon_session_forced_logoff` | `true` | log off a locked session too (a disconnected session is usually locked) |

| `horizon_user_action` | `look` | What to do: look (only show their sessions and desktops), logoff (all their sessions), disconnect (their connected sessions), reset or restart (their desktops), recover (their instant-clone desktops: made again from the image). Never a desktop another user has a session on, nor one in a protected pool. |

## log_analysis

File: `roles/log_analysis/defaults/main.yml`

> LOG ANALYSIS (playbooks/log_analysis.yml for a group of servers, playbooks/vm_log_analysis.yml for vCenter and its ESXi hosts through vCenter's API). Read-only: each host's warning, error and critical log lines of the window, grouped on the AAP side into patterns (the same line with other numbers, times and names is one pattern, counted across hosts), and ACT (GenAI) explains the top ones - likely cause, evidence, fix, confidence - in evidence mode: ACT runs no command anywhere. Every setting can be set for all hosts, per group or host in the inventory, on the template, or as a survey answer (a list may be typed as "a, b" or one per line). docs/LOG_ANALYSIS.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `log_analysis_hours` | `24` | ---- the window ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ The last this-many hours ... |
| `log_analysis_since` | (empty) | ... or a fixed window, e.g. the outage: log_analysis_since "2026-10-23 08:00" and log_analysis_until "2026-10-23 10:30" (UTC, as the report shows times). Since alone = from then until now. |
| `log_analysis_until` | (empty) | the end of the fixed window (empty = now) |
| `log_analysis_source` | `auto` | ---- what to read ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ What a host is: auto (Windows when its connection is WinRM / PSRP, else Linux), linux, windows, or vcsa (a vCenter appliance over SSH: Linux, with the vcsa profile on). Set it per group in the inventory. |
| `log_analysis_profiles` | `[]` | Profiles: one word switches on the logs of a product (roles/log_analysis/vars/main.yml): vcsa, mid_server, iis, sql_server, nginx, httpd, mariadb, podman, sssd, idm, auditd, aap. E.g. for a group of web servers: log_analysis_profiles: [nginx, sssd] |
| `log_analysis_profiles_extra` | `{}` | Your own profiles, or a shipped one changed (the same name replaces it), the shape of vars/main.yml: log_analysis_profiles_extra: {stigman: {files: [/opt/stigman/logs/*.log], units: [stigman-api]}} |
| `log_analysis_priority` | `err` | Linux (and the vCenter appliance): the journal's lines of this priority or worse (journalctl -p: emerg, alert, crit, err, warning, notice). |
| `log_analysis_journal` | `true` | false = no journal (text logs, units and containers only) |
| `log_analysis_units` | `[]` | Units and syslog identifiers whose journal is read at log_analysis_units_priority, lower than the rest: e.g. [sssd, nginx, stigman-api] (globs such as dirsrv@* work) and [sudo, sshd]. |
| `log_analysis_identifiers` | `[]` | syslog identifiers read the same way, e.g. [sudo, sshd] |
| `log_analysis_units_priority` | `warning` | the priority those units and identifiers are read at |
| `log_analysis_containers` | `[]` | Podman containers whose output (podman logs) of the window is read, its lines that match log_analysis_match: a name for root's, user/name for a user's (rootless), e.g. [stigman-api, svc_app/web]. |
| `log_analysis_files` | `[]` | Text logs (globs), read when they changed in the window: their matching lines, the newest log_analysis_max_lines. Compressed rotations (.gz .xz .bz2 .zst) are left out. log_analysis_files is the base list; log_analysis_files_extra adds to it and to the profiles' files (never replaces them). e.g. [/var/log/messages, /v… (all of it: the role file) |
| `log_analysis_files_extra` | `[]` | e.g. [/opt/app/logs/*.log] |
| `log_analysis_become` | `true` | read as root (sudo), as the other checks do |
| `log_analysis_win_logs` | `[System, Application]` | Windows: the event logs read, their critical (1), error (2) and - log_analysis_win_level 3 - warning events. |
| `log_analysis_win_logs_extra` | `[]` | more channels, e.g. ["Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational", "Directory Service", "DNS Server"] |
| `log_analysis_win_level` | `3` | 1 critical, 2 + error, 3 + warning |
| `log_analysis_win_providers` | `[]` | Event providers whose events are read at every level up to information, in the logs above (e.g. [Service Control Manager]); log_analysis_win_providers_only: true = only these providers' events. |
| `log_analysis_win_providers_only` | `false` | true = only those providers' events |
| `log_analysis_win_event_ids` | `[]` | Event IDs always read whatever their level: "Log:ID", or a number for every log read plus Security, e.g. [4625, 4740, "System:7031", "System:7034"]. Security needs an account that may read it. |
| `log_analysis_win_files` | `[]` | Text logs (wildcards), read like the Linux ones; _extra adds to the base list and the profiles', e.g. ['D:\Apps\*\logs\*.log'] (a MID Server's agent logs: the mid_server profile) |
| `log_analysis_win_files_extra` | `[]` | more Windows text logs, added to the list above |
| `log_analysis_match` | `"error\|fail\|fatal\|crit\|panic\|denied\|refused\|timed out\|timeout\|unable to\|cannot\|exception\|…` | The words that make a line of a text log or a container's output worth reading (grep -E, any case); _extra adds words, e.g. [SEVERE, 'HTTP/1.1" 5']. |
| `log_analysis_match_extra` | `[]` | more words, added to log_analysis_match |
| `log_analysis_vcenter_logs` | `[vpxd]` | ---- vCenter and ESXi through vCenter's API (playbooks/vm_log_analysis.yml) ------------------------ No SSH and no login to the hosts: vCenter hands over its own logs and each host's (the "VMware vCenter" credential; a read-only role plus Global > Diagnostics). Keys as vCenter names them. [] = not vCenter's own log |
| `log_analysis_esxi_logs` | `[hostd, vmkernel, vpxa]` | [] = no host logs; more: fdm, vobd, hostd-probe ... |
| `log_analysis_esxi_hosts` | `[]` | host names (* ? allowed); [] = every host |
| `log_analysis_read_lines` | `20000` | read back at most this many lines from the end of each log |
| `log_analysis_max_lines` | `500` | ---- every source ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ keep at most this many lines per log (the newest) |
| `log_analysis_max_line_chars` | `400` | a line longer than this is cut |
| `log_analysis_ignore` | `- 'Event 10016:' # Windows: DCOM "application-specific permission settings" (harmless, by…` | Lines left out everywhere before they are grouped (regular expressions, any case, matched against "<program> <line>"): noise every server logs. log_analysis_ignore is the shipped list; _extra adds yours, e.g. ['sshd.*Connection closed by authenticating user']. |
| `log_analysis_ignore_extra` | `[]` | more lines to leave out, added to log_analysis_ignore |
| `log_analysis_min_count` | `1` | a pattern seen fewer times than this is left out |
| `log_analysis_act` | `true` | ---- ACT ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ACT runs on the AAP side (the execution environment) with the site_act_* settings (roles/site_act/defaults/main.yml); the key comes from an "ACT model key" credential. false = the patterns only, no ACT (no key needed). |
| `log_analysis_question` | (empty) | What you want to know, in your words - ACT looks at it first (a good survey question), e.g. "users report slow logins since 09:00". |
| `log_analysis_names_extra` | `[]` | more names ACT replaces with placeholders before the model sees them (host names are always) |
| `log_analysis_max_items` | `30` | ACT analyzes at most this many patterns, the most severe first (the rest are listed) |
| `log_analysis_act_batch` | `"{{ site_act_batch \| default(5) }}"` | patterns per question to ACT, each with only its evidence (0 = all in one question) |
| `log_analysis_examples` | `3` | example lines per pattern in the evidence, the report and the artifacts |
| `log_analysis_max_chars` | `60000` | the evidence ACT reads is cut at this many characters |
| `log_analysis_check_url` | `true` | first check that the AAP node can reach the model's URL |
| `log_analysis_act_model_timeout` | `"{{ site_act_model_timeout \| default(600) }}"` | Seconds the model may take for its answer: site_act_model_timeout (600) unless set here. |
| `log_analysis_email_if_clean` | `false` | ---- the report ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ The report is printed, kept as the job artifact log_analysis, emailed (report_email_to, and the "Also email the report to" box) and published (report_web_dest). A run that finds nothing is not emailed unless log_analys… (all of it: the role file) |
| `log_analysis_max_rows` | `200` | rows per table in the report (the artifacts have them all) |
| `log_analysis_fail` | `false` | The job stays green when it finds patterns. It fails when ACT was wanted and could not run (after the report), and when no host could be read. true = also fail when a critical or error pattern was found. |

## net_certs

File: `roles/net_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> NETWORK DEVICE CERTIFICATES (playbooks/net_cert_report.yml, net_cert_renew.yml): the TLS certificate each switch, firewall, printer, iLO / iDRAC, UPS, storage ... presents, read from the controller with a TLS hello - no login to the devices, nothing changed. The renewal: a ServiceNow incident per certificate due; on a Cisco IOS / IOS-XE device, optionally a CSR made on the device (net_cert_cisco_csr).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `net_cert_targets` | `inventory` | ---- which devices ---- inventory (the hosts of net_cert_group) / subnets (net_cert_subnets) / both |
| `net_cert_group` | `net_cert_devices` | the inventory group of the devices; a host's own net_cert_ports / net_cert_address / net_cert_servername override |
| `net_cert_ports` | `[443]` | the ports read (a host's own net_cert_ports wins), e.g. [443, 8443, 636] |
| `net_cert_subnets` | `[]` | CIDR ranges to sweep (net_cert_targets: subnets or both), e.g. ['192.0.2.0/24'] - every address, each port in net_cert_ports |
| `net_cert_exclude` | `[]` | never connected to: addresses, CIDR ranges, host name patterns (e.g. ['192.0.2.1', 'ups*']) |
| `net_cert_max_addresses` | `4096` | a sweep bigger than this (all subnets together) is refused: a /16 by mistake would take hours |
| `net_cert_resolve_names` | `true` | a swept address that answers: its DNS name (PTR) in the report, else the address |
| `net_cert_timeout` | `5` | seconds for each connection, and each handshake |
| `net_cert_workers` | `32` | connections at the same time |
| `net_cert_only` | `[]` | only these devices (names, wildcards), e.g. ['sw01*'] - to try the renewal on one |
| `net_cert_warn_days` | `30` | ---- what is due ---- a certificate expiring within this many days is due: a warning incident (amber in the report) |
| `net_cert_crit_days` | `7` | within this many days (or expired): critical |
| `net_cert_notice_days` | `60` | the report colours these blue (a heads-up, no incident) |

## net_config

File: `roles/net_config/defaults/main.yml`

The load (playbooks/net_config_load.yml) sends configuration lines, or restores a backup, after an approved change request - always a dry run (Check) first. Cisco IOS / IOS-XE (over its CLI: network_cli, a Machine credential) and Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (over its XML API from the controller: the "Palo Alto PAN-OS API" credential). docs/NETWORK_CONFIG.md. A backup holds the device's secrets (password hashes, SNMP communities, keys): keep it in a private, internal repository or share only - never in this one.

| `net_config_only` | `[]` | Only these devices (names, * and ? allowed), e.g. [rtr-lab*] - to try a job on one first. [] = every one. |

| `net_config_git_branch` | `main` | the branch (made when the repository is new and empty) |
| `net_config_git_path` | `configs` | the folder in the repository: <path>/<device>.cfg (IOS), .xml (PAN-OS) |
| `net_config_git_author_name` | `site-automation` | the commits' author |
| `net_config_git_author_email` | `site-automation@localhost` | and its email |
| `net_config_git_host_key_checking` | `accept-new` | The git server's SSH host key: accept-new (the first connection learns it), or yes (only the keys in net_config_git_known_hosts - lines as in a known_hosts file). In an execution environment ssh's own known_hosts is empty every job, so accept-new learns the key each time: only net_config_git_known_hosts + yes really c… (all of it: the role file) |
| `net_config_git_known_hosts` | (empty) | the git server's host keys (known_hosts lines), for net_config_git_host_key_checking: yes |
| `net_config_share_dir` | `/var/lib/site-automation/net-config` | The folder for share: on the AAP node (a path AAP exposes to jobs) or on net_config_share_host - <dir>/<device>/<device>.cfg (the latest), and a dated copy beside it each time one changed. |
| `net_config_share_host` | (empty) | an inventory host to keep them on (Linux, or a Windows file server); its credential on the template |
| `net_config_share_keep` | `30` | dated copies kept per device (the oldest go) |
| `net_config_ios_command` | `show running-config` | ---- what is read ---- IOS: the command whose output is kept |
| `net_config_panos_port` | `443` | PAN-OS: the XML API's HTTPS port |
| `net_config_panos_scheme` | `https` | PAN-OS: always https - http is for the tests' stand-in firewall only (it would send the API key in clear) |
| `net_config_panos_validate_certs` | `true` | PAN-OS: check the firewall's certificate |
| `net_config_panos_ca_path` | (empty) | PAN-OS: a CA bundle (PEM) for that check ('' = the system's) |
| `net_config_timeout` | `60` | PAN-OS: seconds per request |
| `net_config_diff_lines` | `60` | lines of a diff shown in the report, the email and an incident (secrets hidden) |
| `net_config_fail_on_failed` | `true` | the backup job fails (red) when a device could not be backed up |
| `net_config_tickets` | `false` | true = an incident when a device's configuration changed (one per change, with the diff) and when one could not be backed up (noted as cleared at the next good backup). The "ServiceNow API" credential. |

| `net_config_panos_entries` | `[]` | PAN-OS: the changes - each {xpath, element, action}: action set (adds or replaces the element's children), edit (replaces the element at the xpath), delete (no element). |

A target may also be set per group or host (net_perf_targets_extr… (all of it: the role file) |
| `net_perf_targets_extra` | `[]` | more targets for some hosts (group_vars / host_vars): added to net_perf_targets |

| `net_perf_loss_warn_pct` | `1` | packet loss from this percent -> warning |
| `net_perf_loss_crit_pct` | `10` | ... from this percent -> critical (100 % = the target does not answer at all) |
| `net_perf_timeout` | `5` | seconds a single ping or connect may wait |
| `net_perf_ocsp` | `[]` | ---- OCSP responders (asked from every host) ---------------------------------------------------------------- Simplest: site_ocsp_certs (below) - a certificate the responder knows, its OCSP address and issuer read from it. net_perf_ocsp, when set, is used instead: a url alone - an OCSP request about a made-up certific… (all of it: the role file) |

| `net_perf_ocsp_warn_ms` | `2000` | an OCSP answer slower than this -> warning |
| `net_perf_ocsp_severity` | `critical` | an OCSP responder that fails: critical (smart card logins fail) or warning |

| `net_perf_errors_warn_per_hour` | `10` | errors per hour (CRC, frame, carrier ...) from this many -> warning |

## servicenow

File: `roles/servicenow/defaults/main.yml`

> SERVICENOW - open, update (and optionally resolve) incidents from check findings, and check that ServiceNow itself (the instance and its MID Servers) is healthy. Uses the REST Table API with ansible.builtin.uri: no extra collection to install. Connection: the "ServiceNow API" AAP credential sets SN_HOST (https://<instance>), SN_USERNAME and SN_PASSWORD in the job's environment. Without it, nothing is sent: the job prints what it WOULD have opened (a safe way to try it out).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `servicenow_min_severity` | `warning` | Findings at or above this severity get a ticket: critical \| warning. A ticket already open stays open while its finding is still there, even below this (the certificate renewal opens one for every CSR) |
| `servicenow_table` | `incident` | the table tickets are opened in (incident) |
| `servicenow_assignment_group` | (empty) | Values for new incidents. Names work (the API is asked to accept display values), e.g. servicenow_assignment_group: Linux Operations |

## site_findings

File: `roles/site_findings/defaults/main.yml`

> Shared by every check playbook. A "finding" is one thing that is wrong on one host:   check:    the check that found it (disk, services, mariadb, ...)   id:       a stable name for this problem on this host, e.g. disk:/var. ServiceNow uses it to             update the same ticket instead of opening a new one every run.   severity: critical \| warning   summary:  one line a person understands ("/var is 96% full (critical at 95%)")   hint:     a read-only command that shows more. A person can paste it into a shell; ACT (when             you add it later) runs it to collect evidence. Check roles only ADD findings. This role starts the list, reports it, and decides pass/fail.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `site_fail_on` | `[critical, warning]` | Which severities make the job FAIL. A failed job is what sends an AAP workflow down its "on failure" path (open tickets, ask ACT, wait for approval). [] = report only, never fail. |
| `site_unreachable_fails` | `false` | A host that cannot be reached (switched off, no network, ssh or WinRM refused, its login refused) in the health checks, the certificate report and renewal, database health, the service watch and troubleshoot: listed as NOT REACHED and left out, and the job is not failed for it. It still counts as checked-for, so the S… (all of it: the role file) |
| `site_syslog` | `true` | One syslog line per finding (tag below), so your log server / SIEM sees them too. |
| `site_syslog_tag` | `site-health` | the syslog tag those lines carry (to filter on in the SIEM) |
| `site_eventlog_source` | `site-health` | Windows: one Application event log entry per finding instead of syslog (source below). |
| `site_os` | `linux` | ---- Linux or Windows (set by the playbook; do not set) ----------------------------------------- Linux playbooks run the roles check_<name>, the Windows ones (win_*.yml) the roles win_check_<name>. |
| `site_check_role_prefix` | `"{{ 'win_check_' if site_os == 'windows' else 'check_' }}"` | check_ (Linux) or win_check_ (Windows): set by the playbook from site_os |
| `site_windows_connections` | `[winrm, psrp, ansible.builtin.winrm, ansible.builtin.psrp]` | How a host is recognized as Windows: its connection, or its shell (Windows OpenSSH). |
| `site_settings_notice` | `true` | A notice in the job output when a project settings file (playbooks/group_vars/*.yml) defines a setting: it wins over AAP's inventory Variables box. false = no notice. |

Needs podman >= 4.4 (Quadlet): RHEL 9.2+ / RHEL 8.8+.

| `stigman_mysql_root_password` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'STIGMAN_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD') }}"` | ---- Secrets: NEVER set these in a vars file or inventory ----------------------------------- They come from AAP credentials (aap/credential_types/*.yml) as environment variables / files on the controller (execution environment). See docs/SECRETS.md. |

## vmware_vm

| `vmware_validate_certs` | `true` | Check vCenter's certificate. false only if the execution environment does not trust your CA yet. |
| `vmware_vcenters` | `[]` | Several vCenters (e.g. Enhanced Linked Mode), one report: the reports and the ESXi security settings read the credential's vCenter AND these (names, or name:port), with the same account. The same vCenter under two names is read once. docs/VMWARE.md, "Several vCenters". e.g. [vc01.yoursite.mil, vc02.yoursite.mil] |

## win_check_accounts

File: `roles/win_check_accounts/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS ACCOUNTS (local accounts; domain controllers have none and are skipped)   - the built-in Guest account is disabled                               -> critical if not   - enabled local accounts: password never expires, password too old,     no logon for a long time                                             -> warning   - members of the local Administrators group that you did not allow     -> warning Names below allow wildcards (* and ?), e.g. 'YOURDOMAIN\Domain Admins', '*\svc_aap'.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_accounts_password_max_age_days` | `60` | an enabled local account's password older than this -> warning (0 = off) |
| `win_check_accounts_inactive_days` | `35` | an enabled local account with no logon for this many days -> warning (0 = off) |
| `win_check_accounts_password_never_expires_allowed` | `[]` | accounts allowed "password never expires" (wildcards) |
| `win_check_accounts_inactive_allowed` | `[]` | accounts allowed to stay unused (wildcards) |
| `win_check_accounts_admins_allowed` | `[]` | Empty = list the members in the job output only. Set it to report anyone else, e.g. win_check_accounts_admins_allowed: ['*\Administrator', 'YOURDOMAIN\Domain Admins', 'YOURDOMAIN\svc_aap'] |

## win_check_certs

File: `roles/win_check_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS CERTIFICATES: every certificate in the machine stores below, and which of them are in use (https bindings of IIS / WSUS / ..., the WinRM HTTPS listener AAP connects through, Remote Desktop). Expiring soon -> warning / critical. Expired: critical when in use, or when it expired less than win_check_certs_expired_report_days ago (older leftovers are only listed in the certificate report).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_certs_warn_days` | `30` | a certificate expiring within this many days -> warning (amber in the certificate report) |
| `win_check_certs_notice_days` | `60` | the certificate report colours these blue (an early heads-up; not a finding) |
| `win_check_certs_crit_days` | `7` | within this many days -> critical |
| `win_check_certs_expired_report_days` | `30` | an expired certificate NOT in use is a finding for this many days after it expired; older ones only in the report |
| `win_check_certs_stores` | `['Cert:\LocalMachine\My', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\WebHosting', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\Remote Des…` | the machine certificate stores read |
| `win_check_certs_trust` | `false` | also every other machine store: Trusted Root, Intermediate CAs, Other People, ... (the certificate report turns it on); with its private key checked as above, without it only listed (trust store) |
| `win_check_certs_trust_skip_stores` | `['Disallowed', 'AuthRoot', 'REQUEST', 'SMS']` | stores never read: the untrusted certificates, the roots Windows Update keeps, pending requests (a CSR's key), the MECM client's own |
| `win_check_certs_remote_desktop` | `false` | false = Remote Desktop's certificates are left out of the report and the renewal (Windows or the GPO renews them): the Remote Desktop store, the one RDP uses, those for Remote Desktop only; true = checked like the others |
| `win_check_certs_ignore_subjects` | `[]` | wildcards, e.g. ['CN=localhost*'] |
| `win_check_certs_endpoints` | `[]` | TLS services whose certificate a client actually gets, e.g. win_check_certs_endpoints: - {name: IIS, host: 127.0.0.1, port: 443, servername: web01.yoursite.mil} |
| `win_cert_renew_dir` | `'C:\ProgramData\site-automation\renew'` | ---- Renewal: a new key and CSR for each certificate that expires soon (playbooks/win_cert_renew_csr.yml) ---- The certificates the Windows certificate report flags (within win_check_certs_warn_days, or expired) that are the server's own - not a trust store's - get a new key and a CSR with the same subject, names and… (all of it: the role file) |
| `win_cert_renew_key_bits` | `2048` | RSA key size, at least 2048 (a bigger old key keeps its size; an EC certificate gets a new key on the same curve) |
| `win_cert_renew_digest` | `sha256` | the CSR's signature: sha256, sha384 or sha512 |
| `win_cert_renew_max` | `10` | at most this many NEW CSRs per server in one run (the rest come the next run) |
| `win_cert_renew_self_signed` | `false` | true = a self-signed certificate gets a CSR too, for the PKI to issue a real one in its place (never one only for localhost) |
| `win_cert_renew_issuer` | (empty) | regular expression: only certificates whose issuer matches (empty = any CA), e.g. 'O=U\.S\. Government' |
| `win_cert_renew_exclude_issuer` | (empty) | regular expression: certificates whose issuer matches are never renewed here (renewed by their own tool) |
| `win_cert_renew_only` | (empty) | regular expression on the certificate's place, e.g. 'used by https' (empty = every one) |
| `win_cert_renew_exportable` | `false` | true = the new key can be exported (to move it to another server); false keeps it on this one |
| `win_cert_install_rebind` | `[https, rdp, winrm]` | ---- Install: the issued certificate (playbooks/win_cert_install_check.yml -> approval -> playbooks/win_cert_install_approved.yml) ---- The PKI's certificate, from the request carrying the CSR (cert_renew_servicenow: catalog), is put together with its pending key by certreq -accept -machine (in Personal); its chain's… (all of it: the role file) |
| `win_cert_install_verify_wait` | `15` | seconds an https port has, after the rebinding, to serve the new certificate (full PowerShell only) |
| `win_cert_restore_backup` | (empty) | ---- Restore: the bindings back on the old certificate (playbooks/win_cert_restore.yml) ---- a backup's folder name, as the restore's Check lists it |
| `win_cert_restore_only` | (empty) | or: the newest backup of each certificate whose thumbprint or subject matches (a regular expression) |

## win_check_disk

File: `roles/win_check_disk/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS DISK: how full each local fixed volume (C:, D:, ...) is.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_disk_warn_pct` | `85` | % used -> warning |
| `win_check_disk_crit_pct` | `95` | % used -> critical |
| `win_check_disk_min_free_gb` | `0` | also warn below this many GiB free (0 = off): big volumes |
| `win_check_disk_overrides` | `{}` | Different limits for particular volumes, e.g. a database volume kept full on purpose: win_check_disk_overrides: 'D:': {warn: 92, crit: 98} |
| `win_check_disk_ignore` | `[]` | volumes not to check, e.g. ['E:'] |

## win_check_eventlog

File: `roles/win_check_eventlog/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS EVENT LOG, the last win_check_eventlog_hours:   - unexpected shutdown or power loss (41, 6008), a crash / blue screen (1001)  -> critical   - disk and file system errors (disk, Ntfs, storage drivers)                    -> critical   - the Security log was cleared (1102)                                           -> critical   - many errors in System + Application (the finding names the top sources)       -> warning   - a System / Application / Security log that is full and not overwriting        -> critical

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_eventlog_hours` | `24` | how many hours back the event logs are read |
| `win_check_eventlog_error_warn` | `50` | this many errors or more in System + Application -> warning |

## win_check_network

File: `roles/win_check_network/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS NETWORK, from the server itself:   - a default gateway and DNS servers are configured;   - the names you list resolve, the TCP services you list answer;   - domain members: the computer's trust with the domain works (nltest /sc_query). A broken     trust is the classic "the trust relationship between this workstation and the primary     domain failed" at logon.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_network_dns_names` | `[]` | Names every Windows server must resolve, e.g. [dc01.yoursite.mil, ldap.yoursite.mil] |
| `win_check_network_tcp` | `[]` | Services every Windows server must reach, e.g. win_check_network_tcp: - {name: LDAPS, host: dc01.yoursite.mil, port: 636} - {name: SIEM, host: siem.yoursite.mil, port: 9997} |
| `win_check_network_secure_channel` | `true` | domain members: test the computer's trust with the domain (nltest /sc_query) |
| `win_check_network_timeout_ms` | `3000` | milliseconds for each TCP test |

## win_check_patching

File: `roles/win_check_patching/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS PATCHING (read-only; installing updates is a later runbook)   - a restart is pending for installed updates (Windows Update, component servicing, ConfigMgr)   - days since the last update was installed (Get-HotFix)   - optional: ask Windows Update which updates are missing (slower; needs full PowerShell)

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_patching_warn_days` | `35` | last update installed this many days ago or more -> warning |
| `win_check_patching_crit_days` | `60` | this many days or more -> critical |
| `win_check_patching_reboot_pending` | `true` | report a restart pending for installed updates |
| `win_check_patching_search_pending` | `false` | also ask Windows Update which updates are missing (slower) |

## win_check_performance

File: `roles/win_check_performance/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS PERFORMANCE: CPU (average of three samples a second apart), memory, page file. The finding names the busiest processes, so you know where to look.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_performance_cpu_warn_pct` | `90` | CPU busy % (average of three samples) -> warning |
| `win_check_performance_cpu_crit_pct` | `98` | CPU busy % -> critical |
| `win_check_performance_mem_warn_pct` | `90` | memory in use % -> warning |
| `win_check_performance_mem_crit_pct` | `97` | memory in use % -> critical |
| `win_check_performance_pagefile_warn_pct` | `80` | page file in use % -> warning |

## win_check_security

File: `roles/win_check_security/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS SECURITY BASELINE (a few high-value STIG items; not a full STIG scan: that is your SCAP / vulnerability scanner)

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_security_av` | `auto` | Antivirus: auto = check Microsoft Defender when it is the active antivirus (skipped when it is passive or off because another product protects the server); defender = always; none = never. |
| `win_check_security_av_signature_max_days` | `7` | Defender's signatures older than this many days -> finding |
| `win_check_security_av_services` | `[]` | Services of your endpoint protection that must run, e.g. Trellix / McAfee: [masvc, mfemms] |
| `win_check_security_firewall_profiles` | `[Domain, Private, Public]` | must be on |
| `win_check_security_smb1` | `true` | SMBv1 must be off |
| `win_check_security_rdp_nla` | `true` | Remote Desktop must require Network Level Authentication |
| `win_check_security_uac` | `true` | User Account Control must be on |
| `win_check_security_legacy_tls` | `true` | TLS 1.0 / 1.1 must be off for incoming connections |

## win_check_services

File: `roles/win_check_services/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS SERVICES   - every required service must be running (critical);   - an automatic service that stopped WITH AN ERROR (exit code not 0) is a warning. Automatic     services that stop cleanly by design (trigger-start, delayed) are not reported;   - a service that crashed several times recently (System log events 7031 / 7034).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_services_required` | `[EventLog, RpcSs, Dnscache, W32Time, WinRM, mpssvc]` | Must be running on every Windows server. Add your own per group with ..._required_extra, e.g. for IIS servers: win_check_services_required_extra: [W3SVC, WAS] |
| `win_check_services_required_extra` | `[]` | more services that must run, e.g. for a group of IIS servers (see above) |
| `win_check_services_ignore` | `- gupdate - gupdatem - edgeupdate - edgeupdatem - MicrosoftEdgeElevationService - GoogleU…` | Automatic services never to report (wildcards allowed: * and ?) |
| `win_check_services_crash_hours` | `24` | look back this far for unexpected stops |
| `win_check_services_crash_warn` | `3` | this many unexpected stops of one service -> warning |

## win_check_time

File: `roles/win_check_time/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS TIME: the Windows Time service runs, syncs with a real source (not the local clock), synced recently, and how far off the clock is from its source. Kerberos (domain logons) fails when a clock is 5 minutes off.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_time_offset_warn_sec` | `1` | seconds off its time source -> warning |
| `win_check_time_offset_crit_sec` | `5` | seconds off -> critical |
| `win_check_time_max_hours_since_sync` | `24` | last successful sync longer ago than this many hours -> finding |

## win_check_trust

File: `roles/win_check_trust/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS TRUST STORES: which still hold a certificate authority that was compromised or that the browsers dropped - the machine certificate stores, the running account's, every Java cacerts and Python certifi bundle found - matched against the trust check's list (roles/check_trust/vars/main.yml, plus check_trust_extra; a severity changed in check_trust_severity). A certificate in the Disallowed store is blocked: listed, no finding. Removal (check_trust_remove: true, on the Windows trust store report): the certificate goes into the Disallowed store and out of the store it was in, Java entries are deleted, certifi bundles cut - each backed up to win_check_trust_backup_dir first. Check mode shows what would go. docs/TRUST_STORES.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_trust_stores` | `['Cert:\LocalMachine\Root', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\CA', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\AuthRoot', 'Cert…` | the certificate stores read (CurrentUser: the account AAP connects with) |
| `win_check_trust_block_stores` | `['Cert:\LocalMachine\Disallowed', 'Cert:\CurrentUser\Disallowed']` | the Disallowed stores: a certificate there is distrusted (blocked) |
| `win_check_trust_java` | `true` | every Java cacerts under the folders below (JKS natively; PKCS12 with the JDK's keytool) |
| `win_check_trust_java_dirs` | `['C:\Program Files\Java', 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Java', 'C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adopti…` | folders searched for cacerts (seven levels deep) |
| `win_check_trust_python` | `true` | every certifi cacert.pem under the folders below |
| `win_check_trust_python_dirs` | `['C:\Program Files\Python*', 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Python*', 'C:\Python*', 'C:\ProgramD…` | folders searched for certifi (seven levels deep) |
| `win_check_trust_backup_dir` | `'C:\ProgramData\site-automation\trust-backup'` | the removal's backups: every certificate and file changed, a folder per run |
| `win_check_trust_timeout` | `60` | seconds for keytool |

## win_patch

File: `roles/win_patch/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS PATCH through the ConfigMgr client: install what Software Center has for the server (the software updates deployed to it), restart if the updates need it, and prove the server came back: every automatic service that was running before runs again. One server at a time by default; the rollout stops at the first server that fails. Check mode lists and changes nothing.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `automatic_restarts` | `false` | NO AUTOMATIC RESTARTS unless you say so: this playbook restarts a server only when automatic_restarts is true (the job template's Variables, or the survey) and the updates need it. With automatic_restarts false (the default) it installs the updates and tells you which servers still need a restart; a person restarts th… (all of it: the role file) |
| `win_patch_serial` | `1` | How many servers are patched at the same time (1 = one by one: the rollout stops at the first server that fails). ONLY in the job template's Variables, a survey or the launch: Ansible picks the batch size before it reads all.yml or any group or host variables, so set there it does nothing. |
| `win_patch_never_reboot_groups` | `"{{ patch_never_reboot_groups \| default(['aap', 'aap_hosts', 'sat', 'netapp', 'netapp_con…` | Servers in these groups are patched but NEVER restarted by this playbook (restart them by hand). Follows the Linux setting (patch_never_reboot_groups) when you set it, so ONE list covers both; the fallback is the Linux role's default (roles/patch/defaults/main.yml; tests/test_protection.py checks it). |
| `win_patch_never_patch_groups` | `"{{ patch_never_patch_groups \| default(['no_patch', 'aap', 'aap_hosts', 'sat', 'netapp',…` | Servers in these groups are skipped entirely (e.g. servers patched only by hand). |
| `win_patch_scan_first` | `true` | ask the client to rescan and re-evaluate before installing |
| `win_patch_scan_wait_sec` | `120` | let that scan settle |
| `win_patch_timeout_min` | `120` | per round: download + install |
| `win_patch_poll_sec` | `30` | how often to look at the progress |
| `win_patch_max_rounds` | `2` | After a restart, look again: servicing-stack and cumulative updates often reveal more updates. |
| `win_patch_restart_delay_sec` | `30` | shutdown.exe /t |
| `win_patch_restart_timeout_min` | `30` | how long the server may take to come back |
| `win_patch_restart_settle_sec` | `30` | after the port answers again, before trying to log on |
| `win_patch_reconnect_pause_sec` | `20` | between logon attempts after the restart |
| `win_patch_services_grace_min` | `5` | After the restart, give delayed-start services this long before calling one missing. |
| `win_patch_services_ignore` | `['gupdate*', 'edgeupdate*', 'MicrosoftEdgeElevationService', 'GoogleUpdater*', 'MapsBroke…` | Automatic services that come and go on their own (wildcards); not compared before/after. |
| `win_patch_winrm_host` | `"{{ ansible_host \| default(inventory_hostname) }}"` | Where AAP reaches WinRM, to see the server go down and come back during the restart |
| `win_patch_winrm_port` | `"{{ ansible_port \| default(5986) }}"` | its WinRM port (5986 = HTTPS) |

## Settings of one host

Set these on the host itself: its host variables in the inventory, or the host's **Variables** box
in AAP. Never in a job template's Variables - there one value would be used for every host. When a
host has none, the role works the value out from the host, so no role file has a default for them.

| Setting | Role | When not set | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net_config_address` | [net_config](#net_config) | the host's `ansible_host`, else its name | The address the backup and load jobs connect to, when it is not `ansible_host` (PAN-OS) |
| `net_config_platform` | [net_config](#net_config) | from `ansible_network_os` | `ios` or `panos`: the platform of a host that has no `ansible_network_os` (`cisco.ios.ios` / `paloaltonetworks.panos`) |
| `net_cert_address` | [net_certs](#net_certs) | the host's `ansible_host`, else its name | The address the certificate report connects to (a host of `net_cert_group`) |
| `net_cert_servername` | [net_certs](#net_certs) | the host's name | The name sent in the TLS hello (SNI): the certificate a device with several names shows for this one |
